context: Provide estimates of hour burden of the collection of information.
Based on current contact volumes, DHS will receive approximately 26,000 redress requests per year.  The annual response population was derived from data compiled from across all program partners.

Travelers seeking redress must complete and submit the TIF (through e-mail, mail, or web portal) to DHS TRIP along with a copy of their U.S. passport or at least one, unexpired, government-issued, and photograph-bearing identification document.  DHS estimates completing the form, including gathering and submitting the required information, will take approximately one half hour (30 minutes).  DHS calculates 13,000 hours as the total estimated annual hour burden for redress applicants.  Respondents are any member of the travelling public; as such, DHS uses the fully-loaded hourly wage rate for all workers, $47.20.  DHS estimates an annual average hour cost burden of $613,600 (or $1,840,800 over the course of the 3-year approval window for this collection).  Table 1 summarizes this calculation.

DHS estimates an annual average hour cost burden of $613,600 (or $1,840,800 over the course of the 3-year approval window for this collection).  Table 1 summarizes this calculation.

DHS estimates for passengers seeking redress that (1) approximately 10 percent (2,600 passengers) will complete an initial website review survey and (2) approximately 10 percent (2,600 passengers) will complete an overall satisfaction survey sent 90 days after case closure.

DHS estimates that survey completion will take approximately 5 minutes for the initial survey and 2 minutes for the overall survey.  Thus, the total estimated annual hour burden for passengers responding to surveys is 303 total hours, or 217 hours (2,600 x 0.0833) for the initial survey and 87 hours (2,600 x 0.0333) overall survey.  DHS utilizes the same wage rate as above ($47.20) to calculate the annual hour cost burden for computing the annual hour burden cost, since only applicants to DHS TRIP would complete the surveys.  DHS estimates an annual hour burden cost of $14,317 ($42,952 for the 3-year period).  Table 2 displays the total estimated hour burden cost for passengers completing surveys.

context: DHS estimates a total annual hour burden and annual hour burden cost by summing the annual hour burden and annual hour burden costs associated with submitting a DHS TRIP application (13,000 hours and $613,600) and the annual hour burden and hour burden costs associated with filling out the surveys (303 hours and $14,317), for a total annual hour burden of 13,303 hours and an annual hour burden cost of $627,917 (39,910 hours and $1,883,752 over the 3-year period).

Provide an estimate of the total annual cost burden to respondents or recordkeepers resulting from the collection of information. (Do not include the cost of any hour burden shown in Items 12 and 14).

DHS estimates the total annual cost burden for travelers applying to DHS TRIP to be approximately $1,261.  The costs to travelers involve costs associated with mailing the TIF and identity documentation.  DHS estimates the cost to mail the documentation is $4.85 via certified mail.  Based on the current volume of forms received by DHS TRIP, TSA estimates that 1 percent of applications to DHS TRIP will continue to be sent via standard mail.  The estimated annual burden for mailing the application is $1,261. Table 3 summarizes these estimates.

context: There are no capital and start-up costs associated with this collection.

Provide estimates of annualized cost to the Federal Government.  Also, provide a description of the method used to estimate cost, and account for other expenses that would not have been incurred without this collection of information.

DHS TRIP does not anticipate costs to the Federal Government for implementing the two surveys beyond expected and usual staff hours.  The cost for the collection of data used in processing redress requests involves cost associated with labor.  TSA uses one full time E-band employee, one full time F-band employee, one full time G-band employee, two full time H-band employees, three full time I-band employee, one full time J-band employee, and one full time K-band employee for this collection (for a total of 10 FTEs).  TSA employee hour burden is calculated by multiplying the 2,087 hours in a Federal employee’s work year and the 10 FTE for an annual TSA employee hour burden of 20,870.  Using a weighted average hourly wage rate of $80.34, TSA estimates the annual hour burden cost to the Federal Government to be $1,676,664 ($5,029,993 million over 3 years).  Table 4 summarizes these estimates.

TSA may mail applications to respondents if needed.  TSA estimates that 5 percent of the 26,000 applicants submit information by mail, or 1,300 respondents.  To mail the applications, TSA estimates the cost is the same as the cost for applicants to mail in the documentation as discussed above, $4.85.  Thus, the estimated annual burden for TSA to mail the application is $6,305.  Table 5 summarizes this estimate.
